children: Demand for US natural gas to be turned into LNG fell on Thursday as feedgas deliveries to Cheniere Energy's
Sabine Pass facility, the largest liquefied natural gas export plant in the country, declined sharply, suggesting at least one liquefaction train may be offline or operating at reduced rates.
• Gas flows to the eight major US LNG export plants fell to 19.3 billion cubic feet per day on Thursday from a revised 19.7 bcfd on Wednesday, according to preliminary LSEG data.

• The decline was driven by lower feedgas deliveries to the Sabine Pass export facility in Louisiana, at just under 4.1 bcfd from the typical level of about 5 bcfd at this time of year, the data showed.
• Most other LNG export facilities were operating near full capacity. The US is the world's largest LNG exporter and a key supplier to Europe and Asia.

• The exception was Freeport LNG in Texas, one of the largest US export terminals, where Thursday marked the 31st consecutive day that it has operated at some level of reduced capacity. Feedgas demand remained around 1.75 bcfd, below the facility's full operating capacity, according to LSEG data.
• Cheniere did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Freeport said its three trains were operating.
• Overall US feedgas demand remained near historically strong levels, supported by robust global demand and high utilization rates across most export facilities.
